sources-and-managed-state.statement: Privileged credentials can be discovered from external identity sources (for example Active Directory or Entra ID) or created locally in the Zscaler Admin Console. Discovered credentials can be moved into a managed state, where Zscaler automatically rotates the passwords, and these managed credentials can be used in future sessions.

quotes: Credentials can be discovered from external identity sources (e.g., Active Directory (AD) or Entra ID) or created locally within the Zscaler Admin Console.
Discovered credentials can be moved into a managed state, where Zscaler automatically rotates the passwords.
These managed privileged credentials can be used in future sessions.

credential-agent-required.statement: Discovering credentials from Active Directory or Entra ID requires a credential agent deployed within the customer infrastructure.

quotes: To discover credentials from an AD or Entra ID, you must deploy a credential agent within your infrastructure.

credential-provider.statement: A credential provider is the external identity source (for example Active Directory or Entra ID) used to discover credentials after the credential agent is set up for a designated identity provider; when one is created, the credential agent application segment can be mapped to that source.

quotes: A credential provider is the external identity source (e.g., Active Directory (AD) or Entra ID) used to discover credentials after you set up the credential agent for a designated identity provider (IdP).
When you create a credential provider, you can map the credential agent application segment to the external identity source.

provider-fields.statement: A credential provider takes a name (which cannot contain special characters other than periods, hyphens and underscores), an optional description, the Provider Agent Application (the credential agent application), an Identity Provider Type (for example Active Directory or Entra ID), and an Internal Identity Identifier, which is the value of the idp_name field of the identity provider agent's JSON file.

quotes: Name: Enter a name for the credential provider. The name cannot contain special characters, with the exception of periods (.), hyphens (-), and underscores ( _ ).
Description: (Optional) Enter a description for the credential provider.
Provider Agent Application: Select the credential agent application associated with the credential provider.
Identity Provider Type: Select the identity provider type (e.g., Active Directory or Entra ID).
Internal Identity Identifier: Enter the value from the idp_name field of the identity provider agent's JSON file.

provider-status.statement: The Credential Providers page shows each provider's credential agent application and a Status of OK (the provider can provide discovered credentials), Error (there is an issue with the provider), Validating (validation in progress) or Pending (validation pending), plus the counts of Saved Queries, New Credentials (discovered), Managed Credentials and Ignored Credentials.

quotes: Application: The credential agent application that has been assigned to the credential provider.
OK: The credential provider can provide discovered credentials.
Error: There is an issue with the credential provider.
Validating: The credential provider is in the process of validation.
Pending: The validation of the credential provider is pending.
Saved Queries: The number of queries saved for the credential provider.
New Credentials: The number of discovered credentials for the credential provider.
Managed Credentials: The number of credentials that are managed for the credential provider.
Ignored Credentials: The number of ignored credentials for the credential provider.

discovery-filters.statement: Discovery filters narrow credential results and can be added from the Managed, Discovered or Ignored tab: a filter names a credential provider, a search query (Discovery) and a filter name. Sync Now discovers credentials using the existing discovery filters, the Sync icon discovers credentials in real time, and Last Synced and Scheduled Sync give the date, time and time zone of the last and next credential pull from the provider.

quotes: You can add discovery filters to privileged credentials to hone the credential results, sync external identity sources (e.g., Active Directory (AD) or Entra ID) to discover credentials in real time, and review the existing discovery filters.
You can add a discovery filter from the Managed, Discovered, or Ignored tab.
Credential Provider: Select a credential provider that you want to add the discovery filter to.
Discovery: Enter a search query to use for the discovery filter.
Name: Enter a name for the discovery filter.
Click Sync Now to discover credentials using the existing discovery filters.
Click the Sync icon to discover credentials in real time.
Last Synced: The date, time, and time zone when the last credential pull from the credential provider occurred.
Scheduled Sync: The date, time, and time zone when the next credential pull from the credential provider occurs.

release-and-discovery-queries.statement: The ZPA release summary lists a PRA credential agent under March 03, 2026 as a feature in limited availability, integrating with Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID for credential discovery. With the agent deployed, credentials are discovered using LDAP queries from Active Directory or search queries from Microsoft Entra, rotation generates new passwords with defined security requirements, rotation policies set the schedules, and filters pull newly created credentials from Active Directory.

quotes: A new credential agent is available for Privileged Remote Access (PRA) that enables ZPA integration with external identity sources, including Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID, for credential discovery.
You can deploy a credential agent to automate the discovery, synchronization, and lifecycle management of privileged credentials for Privileged Remote Access (PRA) in the Zscaler Admin Console.
Automatically discover credentials using LDAP queries from Active Directory (AD) or search queries from Microsoft Entra AD.
Rotate credentials to generate new passwords with defined security requirements.
Create rotation policies to set rotation schedules for credentials.
Apply filters to automatically identify and pull newly created credentials from the AD.
###### Credential Agent Available for Privileged Remote Access
Feature in Limited Availability
evidence.after: To learn more, see Log Streaming Service (LSS) Support for Business Continuity Events.

managed-page.statement: The Managed page lists both local and discovered privileged credentials. Status is the rotation status: Available (discovered credentials that can be used), Local (locally created credentials that can be used) or Rotation Failed (discovered credentials with a failed rotation). Class is the rotation schedule assigned to the credential, and Last Rotation and Next Rotation give the date, time and time zone of the last and next rotation.

quotes: Both local and discovered privileged credentials are displayed.
Status: The rotation status of the privileged credential.
Available: Discovered privileged credentials that are available to be used.
Local: Locally created privileged credentials that can be used.
Rotation Failed: Discovered privileged credentials with a failed rotation.
Class: The rotation schedule assigned to the privileged credential.
Last Rotation: The date, time, and time zone that the privileged credential last rotated.
Next Rotation: The date, time, and time zone that the privileged credential rotates next.

rotate-now.statement: An admin can rotate a privileged credential in real time from the Managed page.

quotes: Rotate the privileged credential in real time.

discovered-page.statement: The Discovered page lists credentials discovered from external identity sources with their Credential Provider, Discovery Filter and the date, time and time zone of discovery. All or specific credentials can be selected to import or ignore; importing offers a Credential Class and a Credential Pool drop-down.

quotes: Select the checkbox next to Name to select all credentials, or select the checkboxes of specific credentials to import or ignore them.
Credential Provider: The credential provider for the discovered credential (e.g., Active Directory, Entra ID, etc.).
Discovery Filter: The filters used to discover the credential.
Discovered: The date, time, and time zone when the credential was discovered.
Credential Class: Select a credential class from the drop-down menu.
Credential Pools: Select a credential pool from the drop-down menu.

ignore-does-not-delete.statement: On the Discovered page the Delete icon moves a credential to the Ignored page, and on the Ignored page it moves a credential back to the Discovered page; neither action deletes the credential from the external identity sources.

quotes: Click the Delete icon to move the credential to the Ignored page. This action does not delete the credential from the external identity sources.
Click the Delete icon to move the credential to the Discovered page. This action does not delete the credential from the external identity sources.

ignored-lifecycle.statement: Credentials discovered through external identity sources that are not currently in use for privileged consoles can be moved from the Discovered or Managed pages to the Ignored page. Credentials on the Ignored page can be moved to the Managed page to use them for privileged consoles, and the Import icon imports an ignored credential.

quotes: You can move credentials discovered via external identity sources (e.g., Active Directory (AD) or Entra ID), that aren't currently in use for privileged consoles, from the Discovered or Managed pages to the Ignored page.
The credentials listed on the Ignored page can be moved to the Managed page if you want to use them for privileged consoles.
Click the Import icon to import an ignored credential.

microtenant-filter.statement: On the Managed, Discovered and Ignored pages the Configured within Microtenant filter option is applied by default to show the privileged credentials configured within that Microtenant, the Global option filters the table to what is configured within the Default Microtenant, and the only available operator is Equals.

quotes: By default, the Configured within Microtenant filter option is applied to show the privileged credentials configured within that specific Microtenant.
The Global option filters the information in the table that is configured within the Default Microtenant.
The only available operator for this filter type is Equals.

credential-class.statement: A credential class is a rotation schedule that can be assigned to rotate the password for a managed credential, and its rotation policy determines when the rotation for a managed credential is triggered.

quotes: A credential class is a rotation schedule that you can assign to rotate the password for a managed credential.
You can set the rotation policy to determine when the rotation for a managed credential is triggered.

rotation-policies.statement: A credential class has a name, an optional description and a rotation frequency (Rotation Policy) of Scheduled, After Each Use or Never. An Interval, an amount plus a type such as Hours, Days or Weeks, appears only when the Scheduled policy is selected. The Credential Classes page shows the number of managed credentials using each class as Members.

quotes: Rotation Policy: The rotation frequency that is set for the credential class (Scheduled, After Each Use, and Never).
Members: The number of managed credentials using this credential class.
Name: Enter a name for the credential class.
Description: (Optional) Enter a description for the credential class.
Interval: Enter the rotation interval amount and select the interval type (e.g., Hours, Days, or Weeks). This option appears only when the Scheduled rotation policy is selected.

rotation-choices.summary: The Managed page words the credential class choices as 30-day rotation, after each use or never; the class pages make the schedule an interval in hours, days or weeks.

quotes: A credential class policy can be applied to managed privileged credentials to control rotation behavior (i.e., 30-day rotation, after each use, or never rotate).

positions.says: The class choices are 30-day rotation, after each use, or never rotate.

quotes: Rotation Policy: The rotation frequency that is set for the credential class (Scheduled, After Each Use, and Never).

positions.says: The Rotation Policy is Scheduled, After Each Use or Never.

quotes: Interval: Enter the rotation interval amount and select the interval type (e.g., Hours, Days, or Weeks). This option appears only when the Scheduled rotation policy is selected.

positions.says: A Scheduled class takes an interval amount and type, for example Hours, Days or Weeks.

rotation-choices.impact: The i.e. wording presents 30 days as the scheduled choice, while the class pages make the schedule an interval of any amount in hours, days or weeks. Do not state 30 days as the only schedule; keep each article attributed.

credential-agent-details.title: What the credential agent is, where it runs and how it is installed
credential-agent-details.detail: The articles and the release summary say only that a credential agent must be deployed within the customer infrastructure. What it is, where and how it is installed, and the identity provider agent's JSON file (whose idp_name field the credential provider form reads) are not described in the captured pages.

discovery-query-syntax.title: Discovery query syntax, drawer Status values and the sync schedule
discovery-query-syntax.detail: The release summary says LDAP queries are used for Active Directory and search queries for Microsoft Entra, with no grammar. The Discovery field is described only as a search query. The status column of the discovery filter list is described with the Discovery Filter text, so its values are unknown, and the interval behind Scheduled Sync is not stated.

interval-limits.title: Credential class interval limits and generated password requirements
interval-limits.detail: The Interval field is described with Hours, Days or Weeks as examples; no minimum or maximum interval is stated, and the release summary's defined security requirements for generated passwords are not described.

provider-error-causes.title: What causes a credential provider Error and what Validating checks
provider-error-causes.detail: The provider status values are defined as there being an issue with the provider, or validation in progress or pending. What causes Error, or what a provider is validated against, is not stated.

local-credential-rotation.title: Whether locally created credentials rotate, and which credentials the Rotate action covers
local-credential-rotation.detail: Rotation is stated for discovered credentials moved into a managed state; locally created credentials show the status Local and the pages do not say whether they rotate. The real-time rotate action is not scoped to discovered or local credentials, and whether After Each Use rotation fires at session end is not stated.
